inspection_summary: Inspected all 665 frozen logical lines (652 LF-delimited physical lines plus 13 form-feed page boundaries). The prose and most displayed mathematics support a coherent componentwise account of bicomplex zeta through the idempotents e1,e2. OCR is adequate for semantic mechanisms but damages several exact coordinate and infinite-product displays, especially lines 370-383, 478-497, 528-537, and 561-613; those formulas must not be treated as transcription-grade without checking the retained PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the construction, bicomplex holomorphicity, RH-equivalence, and Euler-product goals.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates bicomplex numbers as a commutative four-dimensional setting whose zero divisors replace the quaternionic noncommutativity obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Preliminaries
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the bicomplex algebra, invertibility, differentiability, complexified Cauchy-Riemann equations, idempotent coordinates, and componentwise holomorphic representation.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Bicomplex Riemann zeta function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines bicomplex powers and the Dirichlet series, proves componentwise convergence, constructs the maximal holomorphic continuation, proves uniqueness, and locates its polar divisor.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Zeros of zeta(w)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces bicomplex zeros to simultaneous zeros of both complex idempotent components and identifies the trivial-zero lattice.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Bicomplex Riemann hypothesis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Formulates a coordinate condition on nontrivial bicomplex zeros and proves its equivalence to the classical Riemann hypothesis.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Bicomplex Euler product
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Adapts infinite-product convergence to zero divisors and transfers the classical Euler product componentwise.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Hyperbolic Riemann zeta function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Restricts the bicomplex construction to the hyperbolic subalgebra, exhibits nonunique continuation there, and classifies all its zeros as trivial.

accepted_units.title: Commutativity versus zero divisors in choosing a hypercomplex zeta setting
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction identifies the structural tradeoff behind the construction: quaternions avoid zero divisors but are noncommutative, whereas bicomplex numbers are commutative but have zero divisors. This predicts both the ease of defining powers/products and the later need to track a singular divisor.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the full introductory comparison and announced results; it supplies the reason for the representation rather than merely historical decoration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose-supported; no exact formula is needed.

accepted_units.title: Bicomplex algebra and its noninvertible locus
accepted_units.why_material: The four-dimensional commutative algebra is represented as z1+z2 i2 over C(i1), and noninvertibility is characterized by two component conditions. This is the algebraic obstruction governing differentiation, poles, and product convergence later in the source.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the multiplication rules, C2 viewpoint, and Proposition 1 so the zero-divisor locus is not detached from its algebra.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: multiplication and coordinate equations are readable, but exact symbols should be checked against the PDF before faithful quotation.

accepted_units.title: Bicomplex differentiability as coupled complex holomorphicity
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns a difference-quotient notion that excludes noninvertible increments into ordinary holomorphicity of two complex-variable components plus complexified Cauchy-Riemann equations. This is a reusable bridge from an algebra-valued analytic notion to familiar component conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Definition 1, Theorem 1, the Hartogs remark, and the TH(U) formulation; omitting these would hide why later componentwise constructions are holomorphic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the Cauchy-Riemann equations are legible, while the derivative/Jacobian typography at lines 101-103 has extraction noise.

accepted_units.title: Idempotent splitting and componentwise reconstruction of holomorphic maps
accepted_units.why_material: Every bicomplex number splits uniquely into two orthogonal idempotent components, making addition, multiplication, division, invertibility, and holomorphic maps componentwise. Theorems 2 and 3 establish both synthesis from two complex holomorphic functions and decomposition of every bicomplex holomorphic function.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the projection maps and T-cartesian domains required to state the two directions coherently.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High but recoverable: the argument depends on the exact e1,e2 decomposition; line 125-126 typography is damaged and should be verified before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Bicomplex exponentiation reduced to idempotent complex powers
accepted_units.why_material: Defining n^w through the bicomplex exponential makes the Dirichlet series meaningful and immediately exposes its two ordinary complex-power components. This is the construction that connects algebraic representation to analytic convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the exponential definition and its algebraic properties immediately preceding the zeta definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: displayed exponent formulas are mostly readable but retain OCR spacing and superscript risk.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet series convergence as intersection of two complex half-planes
accepted_units.why_material: The bicomplex series is exactly the idempotent sum of two classical zeta Dirichlet series. Its convergence domain is therefore the simultaneous pair of complex half-plane conditions, equivalently a wedge in the original coordinates. This illustrates how componentwise semantics turns a multivariable convergence question into an intersection of scalar constraints.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps Definition 5, Theorem 4, the component calculation, and the coordinate equivalence of domains.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the mechanism is clear, but the exact series and coordinate inequalities should be checked against the retained PDF for transcription-grade use.

accepted_units.title: Componentwise continuation on the complement of the translated zero-divisor set
accepted_units.why_material: The continued bicomplex zeta is assembled from two classical continuations. Identifying the domain as a product of punctured complex planes proves openness and connectedness, componentwise holomorphic reconstruction proves T-holomorphicity, and the several-variable identity theorem yields uniqueness.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Theorems 5-7 because domain geometry, existence, and uniqueness form one mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the set identities and idempotent formula are readable; exact notation for O2 should remain tied to its earlier definition.

accepted_units.title: The complex pole lifts to an entire translated zero-divisor polar set
accepted_units.why_material: Approaching any point where either idempotent coordinate equals the classical pole forces the bicomplex norm to diverge. Thus the excluded set is not an arbitrary technical domain restriction but the maximal obstruction inherited componentwise.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Theorem 8 and the norm-based proof rather than only its conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the proof idea is prose-supported, while the exact norm identity at lines 291-309 should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Bicomplex zeros require simultaneous component zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Orthogonal idempotent components force zeta(w)=0 precisely when both scalar zeta values vanish. Applying the classical trivial-zero set then produces a two-parameter lattice of trivial bicomplex zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the equivalence, Theorem 9, its coordinate derivation, and Definition 6.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium-high: the simultaneous-zero criterion is clear, but the coordinate lattice calculation at lines 321-328 has line-order and fraction noise.

accepted_units.title: A bicomplex zero-coordinate condition equivalent to classical RH
accepted_units.why_material: The proposed bicomplex condition encodes the possibilities in which both idempotent coordinates are zeta zeros, allowing trivial/nontrivial mixtures as well as two nontrivial components. Classical RH implies the listed coordinate loci; conversely a hypothetical off-critical classical zero embeds diagonally as a bicomplex zero that violates them.
accepted_units.context_note: The converse at lines 384-400 is independently legible and is essential: it shows equivalence rather than a one-way reformulation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the exact loci and forward coordinate algebra at lines 346-383 are formula-dependent and substantially fragmented. Preserve only the semantic equivalence until verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Infinite-product convergence adjusted for zero divisors
accepted_units.why_material: The usual nonzero-factor condition is replaced by invertibility of all but finitely many factors and an invertible limiting product. Lemma 1 then proves equivalence with convergence of the two ordinary complex component products.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition, component criterion, and sequence-limit argument; this is the prerequisite for the Euler product rather than routine algebra alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: product symbols and indices are degraded, but the criterion and proof mechanism are recoverable from checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Euler product inherited independently by the two idempotent components
accepted_units.why_material: On the common absolute-convergence domain, the two scalar Dirichlet series admit their classical Euler products; Lemma 1 recombines them into a bicomplex Euler product. The unit demonstrates factorization transfer through a representation that preserves multiplication.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem statement and prose at lines 442-477 establish the result; lines 478-497 contain the intended componentwise recombination but have damaged layout.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: exact prime indices, reciprocal factors, and final displayed equality at lines 445-497 require direct PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Hyperbolic zeta as a real-component restriction of bicomplex zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Restricting to the hyperbolic subalgebra turns the idempotent coordinates into the real values c+d and c-d. The bicomplex construction therefore supplies powers, convergence, Euler product, differentiability, continuation, and a polar set for a hyperbolic zeta without creating a separate analytic mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the classification of two-dimensional algebras only as setup, then the exponential, series, differentiability, and restricted continuation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the conceptual restriction is clear, but the exponential display and especially the series/product formula at lines 518-537 have OCR damage.

accepted_units.title: Hyperbolic holomorphicity does not force unique continuation
accepted_units.why_material: A piecewise real scalar extension is applied separately to c+d and c-d, producing a second D-holomorphic function that agrees with the Dirichlet series on its initial domain and has the same polar behavior. This exposes a sharp limit of importing complex analytic-continuation intuition into a zero-divisor algebra with real components.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the counterexample definition, componentwise difference-quotient check, domain condition, and blow-up argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the existence and role of the counterexample are prose-supported, but the exact piecewise branch at lines 561-566 and displayed limit calculations through line 613 must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Every zero of the hyperbolic restriction is trivial
accepted_units.why_material: Because both idempotent arguments are real, a hyperbolic zero requires two real zeta zeros, which are negative even integers. The rich nontrivial-zero geometry of the bicomplex setting collapses to the previously identified trivial lattice, so no analogous RH remains in this restriction.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the conclusion and short componentwise proof together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the logical reduction is clearly stated; exact lattice typography inherits the formula risk of Theorem 9.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Idempotent decomposition as a transport functor for zeta structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Once bicomplex objects split into two orthogonal complex components, convergence, holomorphic continuation, zeros, and Euler factorization are transported by applying the classical construction separately and recombining.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a within-source structural synthesis, not evidence that every complex-analytic property transfers; zero divisors and domain topology create explicit failures.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero divisors are both the enabling representation and the analytic obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The idempotents created by zero divisors make componentwise analysis possible, while the same noninvertibility forces a translated polar divisor and a stronger definition of product convergence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact norm and product formulas are extraction-risky and need PDF confirmation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Continuation uniqueness depends on the scalar component category
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Complex idempotent components on punctured complex domains inherit identity-theorem uniqueness, whereas the hyperbolic restriction has real scalar components and admits a distinct D-holomorphic continuation agreeing on the original domain.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The precise alternative branch defining the counterexample is OCR-defective at lines 561-566.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Classical RH is recovered by a diagonal bicomplex embedding
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A classical off-critical zero can be embedded with equal idempotent coordinates, turning any violation of classical RH into a violation of the proposed bicomplex coordinate condition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact forward coordinate loci in the bicomplex conjecture require scan verification; only the converse mechanism is transcription-stable.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Restricting the representation can collapse the target phenomenon
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: When idempotent arguments are restricted from complex to real values, simultaneous zeta zeros can only use real trivial zeros, so the nontrivial-zero question disappears rather than yielding a new RH analogue.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This conclusion concerns the source's chosen hyperbolic restriction and definition, not every possible hyperbolic zeta construction.
